# IteratorCountChangesRequiredPosition

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Identify a position-dependent current or key read on a locally allocated finite ArrayIterator after iterator_count consumes it, without rewind or seek. Unknown iterator implementations are excluded.

## Detection

- Report a position-dependent current or key read on a locally allocated finite, non-empty ArrayIterator after iterator_count consumes it, without rewind or seek. Unknown iterator implementations are excluded.
- The count must be an `iterator_count` call that executes on every path to the read. Between the construction and the read, the iterator variable may only appear as an `iterator_count` argument or as the receiver of `current`, `key`, `valid`, `next` or `count`, none of which makes an exhausted cursor valid again. `rewind` and `seek` receivers are also accepted when they precede the last such count, which consumes the iterator again.
- Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods, including imports and supported named arguments. Follow only bounded local facts within one lexical scope. Receiver and argument provenance must establish the specific API contract; variable names and comments never prove intent.
- Report one finding per violating operation. A reachable path, unchanged value identity and applicable API behavior are required. Intervening mutation, unknown calls involving tracked values, escaped aliases or exhausted analysis budgets invalidate proof.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Exclude unresolved required symbols, user-defined lookalikes, incomplete syntax, unknown required values and unsupported versions.
- Both `@custos-ignore IteratorCountChangesRequiredPosition` and `@noinspection IteratorCountChangesRequiredPosition` suppress this native rule.
- Any other mention of the iterator variable between its construction and the read ends the proof, wherever it stands and whether or not it always executes: a `foreach` over the iterator (which rewinds it), a `rewind` or `seek` in a `for` header or a conditional branch, a wrapper such as `new LimitIterator($it)`, an alias, a closure or arrow-function capture, an argument to any other call, an array-access write or another method call.
- An iterator built from an empty array literal: counting leaves it at the same invalid position it started at.

## Fix

None. A repair requires a semantic decision or application error-handling policy.

## PHP versions

Available in PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced API exists. Do not apply extension contracts when the resolved API is unavailable. Gate syntax and version-specific behavior to the configured target.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "IteratorCountChangesRequiredPosition": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore IteratorCountChangesRequiredPosition
```
